          Apple’s position: Apple’s offer to make paper copies available at its San Franciso and Los Angeles offices is to

19        for defendants’ review. Apple did not “refuse” to make those additional laptops available by December 1;
          rather, Apple is providing the laptops, which need to be provisioned and prepared, as soon as it can. Making
20        these paper copies available in Kirkland’s own offices ensures the security of the documents, while providing
          Defendants immediate, additional opportunities to review. Defendants’ specified that Ms. Bennett and Mr.
21        Landes should have access to the paper copies due to an upcoming deposition, but both have had the ability to
          review the at-issue documents already (including this week and last week). Ms. Bennett works in the same
22        building as Kirkland’s San Francisco office, and Mr. Landes is located in LA, where Kirkland also has an office.
          Ms. Bennett has not reviewed the source code computer since November 10, and Mr. Landes has never reviewed
23        the source code computer. Defendants’ proposal, by contrast, would give Ms. Bennett and Mr. Landes full paper
          copies of the source code documents, without restrictions on how the documents are stored and maintained, with
24        whom the documents may be shared, or a requirement regarding the return of the documents.
25        Defendants’ position: Apple’s offer to make additional paper copies available at its offices is not sufficient and

26        designee on Apple’s alleged trade secrets (and thus, these documents) on Wednesday, December 3, 2025. Thus,
          counsel needs reasonable access to these documents in advance of taking this deposition. Defendants requested
27        that the Seventeen Documents be delivered on the source code laptop by Monday, December 1, 2025, which

                                  14            Plaintiff Apple Inc. (“Apple”) and defendant Guangdong Oppo Mobile

                                  15   Telecommunications Corp., Ltd. (“OPPO”) ask the Court to resolve their dispute concerning

                                  16   OPPO’s document production. Dkt. No. 142.1 The Court held a hearing on this dispute on

                                  17   November 18, 2025. Dkt. No. 161.

                                  18            The parties’ joint submission addresses two disputes: (1) whether OPPO has withheld

                                  19   from production documents that are otherwise responsive to Apple’s RFPs 2 and 4 based on

                                  20   OPPO’s unilateral determination that the documents contain information that does not qualify as

                                  21   trade secret; (2) whether OPPO must produce documents supporting or used to prepare its answer

                                  22   to Apple’s Interrogatory No. 2. Dkt. No. 142 at 1. Each dispute is addressed separately below.

                                  23            1. With respect to RFPs 2 and 4, for the reasons explained in more detail during the

                                  24   hearing, the Court is not persuaded that OPPO has used a review methodology that filters out

                                  25   otherwise responsive documents based on OPPO’s own determination that the contents of a

                                  26
                                  27   1
                                        The Court will issue a separate order regarding Apple’s motions to seal a portion of the
                                  28   discovery letter and certain appended exhibits (Dkt. Nos. 143, 144).
                                         Case 5:25-cv-07105-EKL          Document 166         Filed 11/19/25     Page 2 of 2




                                   1   particular document are generally known to those in the relevant industry or for some other reason

                                   2   do not qualify as “trade secret.” While OPPO is not required to produce documents that are

                                   3   obviously already public (e.g., a published article), for the avoidance of doubt the Court orders

                                   4   that OPPO must not rely on a review methodology that filters out otherwise responsive documents

                                   5   based on OPPO’s own determination that the contents of a particular document do not qualify as

                                   6   trade secret, and if it has used such a methodology, OPPO must immediately correct this error. If

                                   7   they have not already done so, the Court encourages the parties to confer about specific examples

                                   8   that Apple believes should have resulted in the production of responsive documents. See Dkt. No.

                                   9   142, Exs. 3 and 4.

                                  10          2. With respect to Interrogatory No. 2, no Rule or court order requires OPPO to produce a

                                  11   document simply because it supports or was used to prepared OPPO’s interrogatory answer.

                                  12   OPPO does not rely on Rule 33(d), even implicitly. Apple concedes that no document request
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13   requires this production. For these reasons, Apple’s request for an order requiring OPPO to

                                  14   produce these documents is denied.

                                  15          IT IS SO ORDERED.

                                  16   Dated: November 19, 2025
